title: From text to design: a framework to leverage LLM agents for automated CAD generation

model.params_source: assumed (the paper states no decoding parameters; it only says ChatGPT-4 Turbo was used through its API with function calling)

task.subset_rule: paper-defined: 4 test geometries (box, corner plate, u-profile, toy car) x 15 attempts = 60 runs under the stepPlanning agent workflow; each geometry is described by 3 distinct textual prompts
task.approximation: an agentic multi-turn loop with function calling into a CAD kernel, not a single chat completion; the runner cannot execute it

items.source: https://github.com/R-SMP/text-to-design (Appendix A: 'The code for framework, including the predefined set of prompts and the experimental data, can be found here'); repository reachable 2026-09-19 (HTTP 200)
items.config_or_split: the predefined prompt set for the four test geometries
items.license: unknown (not read; the repository was only checked for existence)

prompt.source_location: Appendix A - which contains no prompt text, only the repository link; Fig. 1 shows the flowchart with a 'predefined context' and a 'function call file' as separate inputs
prompt.verbatim: none (no prompt is printed in the paper; the three textual prompts per geometry, the stepPlanning instruction and the function-call schema all live in the repository only)

output.postprocess: the agent emits function calls that are assembled into a CAD script; the artefact, not the text, is scored
output.parse_paper: the workflow terminates when the model returns the Finished function; the generated geometry is then rendered

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: success rate = successful attempts / attempts, where an attempt counts as successful only if the part was generated, complete and accurate under a binary success/failure visual inspection (Sec. 4.1, Fig. 2b)
metric.judge: human (binary visual inspection of the rendered geometry against the ground-truth CAD model)
metric.original_location: Table 2 (stepPlanning workflow), row GPT-4 Turbo, Total column: 26/60 (43%); the same 26/60 also appears as the stepPlanning row of Table 1

open_points: prompt not printed: Appendix A is a bare repository link, so the three prompts per geometry and the agent-workflow system messages would have to be taken from github.com/R-SMP/text-to-design rather than from the paper.

environment: the framework drives a CAD kernel through function calls and assembles the geometry in Rhino/Grasshopper; reproducing a run means standing up that toolchain, which is outside the runner and needs a licensed CAD environment.
judge: success is a human binary visual inspection of the rendered part against the Fig. 2a ground truth; there is no automatic scorer in the paper.
notes: GPT-4 Turbo also has a Table 1 cell (111/240 across all four agent workflows) and Table 3/4 cells for the FCRC bracket case study; all of them are scored the same way. The FCRC bracket additionally needs topology optimisation in Rhino/Grasshopper with the tOpos plugin.
